facts.text: The strongest simulation safety argument is not that simulation replaced physical testing, but that physical testing established truth anchors and boundaries for simulation use.
facts.quote: The strongest possible argument is therefore not "simulation replaced physical testing". It is: physical testing established the truth anchors and boundaries;

facts.text: The strongest simulation safety argument includes independent validation showing that simulation predicts safety-relevant quantities with quantified uncertainty inside boundaries established by physical testing.

facts.text: After physical testing establishes boundaries and independent validation establishes predictive credibility, the strongest safety argument uses the simulation model to cover the otherwise infeasible combinatorial interior.

facts.text: The strongest simulation safety argument retains targeted physical confirmation at high-risk boundaries and after influential changes.

facts.text: The pattern of physical truth anchors and boundaries, independent simulation validation with quantified uncertainty, simulation coverage of the combinatorial interior, and targeted physical confirmation is recognizable across FAA certification by analysis, rail virtual acceptance, nuclear evaluation-model validation, FDA V&V 40 and UNECE automated-driving assessment.
